security_spec.violation_condition: The XiangShan RTL implementation of the Smip fast-interrupt handler instructions (ipopxresprestore on trap entry, ipopxret on trap exit) still executes the conditional stack-pointer swap micro-operations (cspspush sp / cspspop sp) that were removed from the spec. Specifically, during ipopxresprestore, the hardware reads the xsp CSR and swaps it with sp, saving the interrupted context's registers to the swapped-in interrupt stack instead of the interrupted context's own stack. During ipopxret, the hardware performs the reverse swap before xret, restoring the original sp from xsp. This stale behavior persists if the Chisel-generated RTL or microcode ROM for these pseudo-instructions was not updated to match the spec change.
security_spec.summary: Stale cspspush/cspspop stack-swap micro-ops in Smip trap entry/exit instructions cause interrupted context to be saved on an attacker-controlled interrupt stack instead of the victim's own stack, enabling privilege escalation via stack-pointer hijack

location.function_name: N/A — Smip not implemented in XiangShan

findings.finding: XiangShan RTL (kunminghu-v3 branch, HEAD 4bfb226b) does not implement the Smip fast-interrupt extension at all. No Smip instructions (ipopxret, mipopret, sipopret), no CSPS conditional-stack-swap micro-ops (cspspush/cspspop), no mspcs/sspcs CSRs, and no Smip trap-entry/exit FSM exist in the codebase. Therefore the stale conditional-stack-swap behavior described in PR #691 cannot be present — there is no implementation to be stale. The spec_ref document at riscv-fast-interrupt/src/aclic.adoc lines 1482 and 1504 still retains the pre-PR#691 cspspush/cspspop in its trap-entry/exit sequences (this appears to be the unpatched spec_ref copy), but since XiangShan has no corresponding RTL, there is no hardware-level violation.

spec_citations.excerpt: Pre-PR#691 trap entry: 'Conditionally performs a stack pointer swap by executing xcspspush sp'. Pre-PR#691 return: 'Conditionally performs a stack pointer swap by executing xcspspop sp'. PR #691 (riscv/riscv-fast-interrupt#691, merged 2026-01-06) removes both, saving context on interrupted context's own stack.
Removes cspspush from trap entry, cspspop from trap exit, and cspspop sp,sp from ipopxret pseudocode. Adds NOTE: 'Intentionally, the context is saved on the stack owned by the interrupted context.'
